scope: Complete exact Han2610.01202v1 main-source first/automatic second reading and twenty actual PDF-page inspections; three direct Hermitian entropy proofs in an inactive fragment.
mathematical_boundary: Fixed-volume logarithmic flow: torsion identity for convex entropies; monotonicity when every evolved metric is Gauduchon, including Gauduchon surfaces and invariant-mass backgrounds; all-target initial power-entropy criterion equivalent to the Gauduchon identity. No existence, convergence, uniform degeneration estimate, novelty, or original-problem closure is claimed.

proof_obligations: Keep the denominator M fixed and distinguish it from a time-dependent mass normalization.
Restrict every flow assertion to an assumed smooth positive solution interval.
Differentiate log density using the explicit n-normalized linearized operator.
Convert the fixed target measure to the evolving volume before integration by parts.
Verify both complex-Hessian and gradient coefficients in the scalar chain rule.
Transfer dd^c to the background power using the retained Stokes lemma with positive sign.
Check additive-constant invariance of G by vanishing total integral of the torsion form.
Check both p-entropy coefficients and their exponents for every p>1.
Establish mass preservation under evolved Gauduchon forms directly, with initial value one.
Use positivity of dr wedge d^c r for convex entropy dissipation.
Use strict convexity, positive background and connectedness for the exact equality case.
Pass power entropy to its Lp norm without altering the fixed probability target.
Verify persistence on surfaces and under all background-power identities.
Keep higher-dimensional initial Gauduchon identity distinct from persistence.
Define the initial derivative by a positive short path without claiming that path solves the flow.
Check the path has the required parabolic velocity at zero.
Express the nonzero torsion top form as f times normalized reference volume.
Use zero mean of f and strict positivity of its square integral.
Normalize the varying target probability exactly using c_epsilon.
Check c_epsilon has no first-order term, the torsion term has positive first-order coefficient, and the gradient term is quadratic.
Separate direct entropy derivations from Han full uniform Skoda and Green-function dependency chains.
